question: Who among the following freedom fighters was one of the founders of the Fergusson College in Pune in 1885?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak **was one of the prominent leaders of the **Indian independence movement**, who played a crucial role in inspiring the masses to fight against British rule.
 
• He was also a social reformer and educationist, who believed in the importance of education for the progress and empowerment of the masses.
 
• In 1885, along with other like-minded individuals, Tilak founded the Deccan Education Society, which established the Fergusson College in Pune.
 
• The Fergusson College was named after Sir James Fergusson, the Governor of Bombay at that time, and was one of the first institutions of higher education in India to offer courses in science and liberal arts.
 
• The college played a significant role in promoting modern education and creating a new generation of educated and enlightened Indians who could contribute to the nation-building process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Subhash Chandra Bose: Subhash Chandra Bose was a freedom fighter and nationalist leader who played a key role in the Indian independence movement. However, he was not associated with the founding of Fergusson College in Pune.
 
• Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel: Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and the first Deputy Prime Minister of India. However, he was not involved in the establishment of Fergusson College.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai: Lala Lajpat Rai was a prominent nationalist leader and freedom fighter who played a crucial role in inspiring the masses to fight against British rule. However, he was not one of the founders of Fergusson College in Pune.
